doc_name: List of prime ministers of Japan
text: The prime minister of Japan is the head of government and leader of the Cabinet. This list covers all prime ministers from the first in the modern sense, Itō Hirobumi, who took office in 1885, to the present day. Under the Meiji Constitution, 32 prime ministers held office with a mandate from the Emperor; however, the "electoral mandates" listed refer to the House of Representatives, the lower house of the Imperial Diet, which was not constitutionally guaranteed to influence the prime minister's appointment. Currently, the prime minister is selected from among members of the National Diet and appointed by the Emperor following nomination by the Diet. Prince Naruhiko Higashikuni held office for only fifty-four days in 1945, making it the shortest premiership in Japanese history, while Shinzo Abe served the longest, totaling eight years across two non-consecutive terms. As of 20 October 2025, Sanae Takaichi is the current prime minister. The office of daijō-daijin, historically equivalent to the prime minister, was an ancient position discontinued in the 18th century and briefly revived during the Meiji era. It was formally abolished in December 1885 with Itō Hirobumi's appointment as the first prime minister (naikaku sōri-daijin). As of 20 January 2026, eleven former prime ministers are still alive. The most recent death was that of Tomiichi Murayama (1994–1996), who passed away on 17 October 2025 at the age of 101, having become a centenarian on 3 March 2024.
